A former OpenAI researcher walked away from $2M to speak freely about AI risk. Researchers still inside the labs
say his scenario feels accurate. Here’s the full map.

12 min read
Just now

--

In August 2021, before ChatGPT existed, a researcher laid out what AI would look like in 2026. He got most of it right. Then he left OpenAI, refused to sign a non-disclosure agreement, and published his next forecast. Here is what it says — and why the people still inside the labs think it is broadly correct.
In August 2021, a researcher named Daniel Kokotajlo published a blog post. It was titled “What 2026 Looks Like.”
At the time, ChatGPT did not exist. GPT-4 did not exist. The AI boom that would restructure entire industries and consume the conversation of everyone from hedge fund managers to primary school teachers was still more than a year away. The post was read by a small community of AI researchers and forecasters. Most people had never heard of OpenAI.
Kokotajlo wrote that by 2026, AI would use chain-of-thought reasoning. This is the ability to think through problems step by step. He predicted AI training runs would cost $100…
